title: Lesson 14 · The Verb in Depth II
blurb: Helping verbs, regular vs irregular, principal parts, progressive/emphatic/interrogative forms, and verb mistakes.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“I have gone home.”
items.explain: “have” helps form the tense — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“She will sing tonight.”
items.explain: “will” helps form the future — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“You must go now.”
items.explain: “must” helps the main verb “go” — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“He is running fast.”
items.explain: “is” helps form the progressive — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“They do work hard.”
items.explain: “do” helps the main verb “work” — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“I can swim well.”
items.explain: “can” helps the main verb “swim” — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“We shall win.”
items.explain: “shall” helps form the future — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the helping (auxiliary) verb?

“It may rain soon.”
items.explain: “may” helps the main verb “rain” — the auxiliary verb.

items.prompt:
Is this verb regular (adds -ed) or irregular (changes form)?

“walk”
items.explain: walk → walked → walked; adds -ed — regular.

items.prompt:

items.prompt:
Which coordinate form is this — progressive, emphatic, or interrogative?

“I am writing.”
items.explain: “am writing” shows action going on — progressive form.

items.prompt:

items.explain: “do love” adds emphasis — emphatic form.

items.prompt:
Which coordinate form is this — progressive, emphatic, or interrogative?

items.explain: “Do you write” asks a question — interrogative form.

items.prompt:

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“The man ___ a stone.”
items.explain: “throw” is irregular: the past is “threw,” never “throwed.”
